Readwise Reader's Ghostreader AI runs on a credit system that can cap out before your monthly reset — that's the kind of detail that doesn't show up on the pricing page.

Readwise Reader is the read-it-later app from the team behind Readwise's highlight-syncing tool, and it's built for people who read a lot of stuff scattered across a lot of places — articles, PDFs, newsletters, RSS feeds, X/Twitter threads, YouTube transcripts, EPUBs. It all lands in one inbox instead of six browser tabs and three apps.

A few specifics worth knowing before you consider it:

→ $9.99/month billed annually ($119.88/year) for the Full plan, which includes Reader. Month-to-month bumps it to $12.99/mo. A cheaper Lite tier ($5.59/mo) exists but drops Reader entirely — it's highlights-only.
→ Ghostreader, the built-in AI, summarizes articles and answers questions about documents as you read. It's genuinely useful for deciding whether a long piece is worth your time, but it's an LLM reading one document at a time — not a research tool.
→ The reading interface is keyboard-first, with vim-style j/k navigation for people who'd rather not touch a mouse.
→ Highlights feed into Readwise's spaced-repetition flashcard system, so something you highlighted months ago can resurface later instead of disappearing into a note you never reopen.
→ Students and academics get 50% off any plan, verified.

Worth flagging honestly: there's no permanent free tier after the 30-day trial, no team plans (it's built for individuals), and recent third-party reviews average 3.64/5, with people citing Ghostreader's credit caps and occasional performance issues.
